groups.title_vi: Sàn gỗ phòng ngủ
groups.subject_en: The bedroom's real floorboards, seen from directly above: grey-brown six-inch-wide wooden planks running east-west with staggered butt joints, grain, small nail heads and ordinary scuffs. It is the floor around the rug, the toy mats and the furniture; it is the 'real world' under the imagined kingdom, so it is plain and quiet.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Planks always run east-west and every variant has the same board width (about 12 px) so mixed variants line up; joints sit at different positions per variant.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).
groups.palette_en: floorboard grey-brown #8A7A66 (shade #6F6252, light #A39378), nail heads #5B5043, joint lines #54493D, warm sun #F2D79A (light patch only), void blue-black #14131C.
groups.notes_vi: 8 biến thể sàn gỗ, các tấm gỗ chạy ngang, ghép liền mạch. Bước chân trên các ô sàn gỗ này dùng âm step_wood (assets/sfx/pawn/step/step_wood_01..04.wav); bụi dùng step_dust_wood.

groups.title_vi: Cầu phấn của đứa trẻ (Chalk Path)
groups.subject_en: The child's Chalk Path: a temporary bridge of crayon-blue chalk the huge hand draws across gap cells (up to 3 in a straight line) so the pawn can walk across. It looks hand-drawn and waxy: rough parallel strokes of crayon-blue forming a flat bridge surface, edges of chalky white dust, a few stray strokes. The bridge is the one place on the board that is unmistakably the child's, so its crayon-blue is the most saturated colour in a room. This group owns the whole bridge cell: stills, end caps, draw-on, the 3-second fade warning and expiry (the old vfx chalk_path_* overlays were removed as duplicates).
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). The bridge runs through the tile along its axis and fills the full width; on the two open long sides a 3-4 px strip of dark void is visible beneath the chalk with a thin crayon-blue edge. Tiles join end to end seamlessly (mid pieces). Strokes are visible, not smoothed: at least 6 distinct crayon strokes per tile. Cell kind chalk: walkable.
groups.avoid_en: No planks, no wood grain, no nails (it is drawn, not built). No red. No hand in the tile.
groups.palette_en: crayon blue #3A6FE0 (light #8DB0F0, dark #284CA0), chalk white #EAF0FA, void blue-black #14131C, paper dust #CFD6E6.
groups.notes_vi: Cầu phấn màu xanh sáp, thấy rõ nét vẽ; ghép nối đầu-đuôi.

groups.title_vi: Ô sàn - Thảm cờ vua
groups.subject_en: The chessboard play-rug that lies on the child's bedroom floor, the battlefield of the imagined war: a woven wool rug printed as a chessboard. Squares alternate warm ivory (never pure white) and soft charcoal-slate (never pure black). Seen from above you read a felted pile with a faint weave, threadbare patches, repaired seams stitched with coarse pale-blue cloth thread and the odd waxy smudge. It must feel handled, tidy-ish and a little sad, like a toy rug after a long game.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). A checkerboard needs two kinds of square: every 'light' tile is ivory and every 'dark' tile is slate, and the two kinds meet seamlessly in any order. The weave texture is identical across variants so only the wear differs.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).
groups.palette_en: ivory #E6DAC0 (shade #CDBF9F), charcoal-slate #3F3D4A (shade #2E2C38); accents only on borders: faded burgundy #7A3B45 and dull gold #B79A55; repair thread pale blue #8FA6C4; wood border dark walnut #4A3626.
groups.notes_vi: Ô sàn bàn cờ: 'light' và 'dark' phải ghép xen kẽ được. Mỗi ô 32x32, không viền.
groups.used_in: Act 1 rooms t1-t4, b1 and the hub h1 (Chess Rug)

groups.title_vi: Mép và góc sàn - Thảm cờ vua
groups.subject_en: Floor edge and corner tiles for the chess rug: they close a floor region against the out-of-board area where there is no wall (the floor's own border). Border material: the rug's border: a band of faded burgundy with a thin dull-gold stripe and short fringe tassels at the very edge, lying on a dark line of shadow.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Edge naming: the suffix is the SCREEN side where the floor area ENDS (the floor continues away from that side). Corner tiles combine two sides. Inner corners are concave bends. All twelve must line up with each other and with the floor tiles on every continuing side.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).
groups.palette_en: ivory #E6DAC0 (shade #CDBF9F), charcoal-slate #3F3D4A (shade #2E2C38); accents only on borders: faded burgundy #7A3B45 and dull gold #B79A55; repair thread pale blue #8FA6C4; wood border dark walnut #4A3626.
groups.notes_vi: 12 ô: 4 mép, 4 góc ngoài, 4 góc trong. Ghép liền với ô sàn ở mọi phía còn lại.

groups.title_vi: Tường - Thảm cờ vua
groups.subject_en: Solid wall tiles for the chess rug. Cap tiles are the top surface seen from above; face tiles are the short front (south-facing) vertical face that sits one row under a cap row. A north wall is one or more cap rows plus one face row; a south wall shows caps only. Wall material: the top of the dark-walnut wooden frame that borders the chessboard: a bevelled top surface with a thin inlaid ivory line, slightly worn corners and tiny nail heads; face: the short front face of the dark-walnut board frame: vertical wood grain, a narrow routed groove near the top, a few scuffs, sitting on the rug's shadow.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Caps: wall_cap_a/b are the fill; edge_<side> has its outer rim on that side; corner_<dir> is an outer corner; inner_<dir> is a concave corner. Faces: a, b, c are interchangeable variants; face_end_w/e close a free end. Every wall tile is solid.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).
groups.palette_en: ivory #E6DAC0 (shade #CDBF9F), charcoal-slate #3F3D4A (shade #2E2C38); accents only on borders: faded burgundy #7A3B45 and dull gold #B79A55; repair thread pale blue #8FA6C4; wood border dark walnut #4A3626.
groups.notes_vi: 19 ô tường: mũ (2 + 4 mép + 4 góc ngoài + 4 góc trong), mặt (3) và 2 đầu mặt. Tất cả là vật cản.

groups.title_vi: Hố / khoảng trống - Thảm cờ vua
groups.subject_en: Gap (hole) tiles for the chess rug: cells the pawn cannot walk onto but can leap over with Rule Step or bridge with the child's Chalk Path. The gap here is a square torn clean out of the rug: frayed rug edges and loose threads around a dark hollow that drops to cold blue-black shadow beneath the rug, with the faint grey of floorboards far below.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Gaps never look like a floor: they are the darkest value in the district. Lips are drawn in the district's lip material. In the game camera you see the FAR (north) inner wall of a pit as a shaded vertical face about 10 px tall; the near (south) wall is hidden, so a south lip is only a thin 2-3 px highlight. End tiles (gap_end_<side>) close a trench on the named side: floor on three sides, the gap continues on the fourth. Inner-corner tiles (gap_inner_<corner>) are the concave counterpart of the outer corners: all four edge neighbours are gap and only the named diagonal neighbour is floor, so only a small notch of lip appears in that corner. Painted together with the outer corners they let any 2- or 3-cell trench and any L-, T- or plus-shaped pit be built without an open, unlit edge.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).
groups.palette_en: ivory #E6DAC0 (shade #CDBF9F), charcoal-slate #3F3D4A (shade #2E2C38); accents only on borders: faded burgundy #7A3B45 and dull gold #B79A55; repair thread pale blue #8FA6C4; wood border dark walnut #4A3626.
groups.notes_vi: 21 ô hố: 2 ô giữa, 4 mép, 4 góc ngoài, 4 đầu mút (rãnh 3 mặt), 4 góc trong, 1 hố đơn, 2 dải. Là ô cấm đi bộ nhưng nhảy qua được. Đầu mút và góc trong cho phép ghép rãnh 2-3 ô và hố hình L/T mà không hở mép.

files.name: gap_inner_ne.png
files.what_en: Inner (concave) corner of a gap region, floor only on the diagonal NORTH-EAST: the north, east, south and west neighbours are all gap. In the north-east corner draw a small notch of floor about 8x8 px whose inner edge is rounded concave toward the pit, in the lip material (the torn, frayed rug pile with pulled threads and a thin darker backing edge) with a 2-3 px lit rim. Directly beneath the notch the pit's far inner wall face (about 10 px tall) continues from the neighbouring east tile across the notch's 8 px width and ends in a stepped, rounded cut, so the wall face appears to wrap round the corner. Everything outside the notch is gap void with the interior and depth described in the SUBJECT. Every edge of the tile continues into gap and must match the edges of a gap centre tile.

Directly beneath the notch the pit's far inner wall face (about 10 px tall) continues from the neighbouring west tile across the notch's 8 px width and ends in a stepped, rounded cut, so the wall face appears to wrap round the corner. groups.title_vi: Vật che chắn / khối nhảy qua - Thảm cờ vua
groups.subject_en: Low cover tiles for the chess rug: solid obstacles the pawn cannot walk through but can leap over (cell kind leapable_block); they stop Rook charges and straight beams. Each reads as a district object sitting ON a floor tile.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). The tile includes its own plain floor underneath (this tile replaces the floor cell) and the object is low enough that a character behind it stays readable. A short south front face shows the object's height (about 8-10 px).
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).

groups.subject_en: Exit, gate and one-way shortcut tiles for the chess rug, in open and locked states (locks are visible BEFORE they open and must read as 'blocked, and here is roughly why'). Locked and closed states are solid; open states are walkable floor.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Exit tiles sit in the room's wall ring: the wall, the opening and the floor continue seamlessly with this district's wall faces and floor tiles. groups.subject_en: Seam tiles where the chess rug meets its neighbouring districts and the bedroom floor. They let rooms and the world map blend materials without hard cuts.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. groups.title_vi: Thảm đường rước (runner) - Thảm cờ vua
groups.subject_en: The kingdom runner: a woven ceremonial strip laid over the chess rug, leading from the room's centre to the fallen White King and onward. Faded burgundy centre field with two dull-gold edge stripes, a small woven diamond pattern in ivory thread, slightly raised edges and a soft shadow on the rug. It is the only 'kingdom red' in Act 1 - an old, faded cloth, never a saturated red, so it never competes with damage red.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). The runner is exactly one cell wide: its gold edge stripes sit 3 px inside the left and right (or top and bottom) edges and a 2-3 px shadow strip shows the rug at those two edges. Straight pieces join end to end seamlessly. Walkable floor. Corner pieces (runner_corner_<edge><edge>) turn the strip through 90 degrees between the two named edges; T pieces (runner_t_<side>) have a branch to the named side and a closed opposite edge.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).
groups.palette_en: faded burgundy #7A3B45 (shade #5E2C36), dull gold #B79A55, ivory fringe #E6DAC0, shadow on rug #2E2C38.
groups.notes_vi: Mảnh thảm đường rước 1 ô rộng: thẳng nối đầu-đuôi, 4 đầu mút, 4 góc rẽ và 4 ngã ba để trải đường uốn lượn (T1 dài 28 ô trở lên).

groups.title_vi: Huy hiệu trung tâm hub - Thảm cờ vua
groups.subject_en: The central medallion woven into the Chess Rug hub (room h1): a 2x2-cell emblem, a ring of dull gold with a small ivory pawn silhouette in its centre and four tiny stars around it, set into the ivory and charcoal squares. It gives the hub a centre point the child's gifts (shelter, banners, train) are arranged around. The four files are the four quarters of one medallion.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Quarter naming: nw/ne/sw/se is the quarter's position in the 2x2 emblem. The four tiles must join with no visible seam and the pawn silhouette is cut exactly at the 2x2 centre. Walkable floor.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).
groups.palette_en: ivory #E6DAC0 (shade #CDBF9F), charcoal-slate #3F3D4A (shade #2E2C38); accents only on borders: faded burgundy #7A3B45 and dull gold #B79A55; repair thread pale blue #8FA6C4; wood border dark walnut #4A3626.
groups.notes_vi: 4 phần tư của huy hiệu 2x2; phải khớp tuyệt đối ở giữa.

groups.subject_en: The Toybox kingdom floor: a meadow-green felt play-mat seen from above, soft short nap with fine fibres and tiny pills, slightly darker where it has been trodden. It is the grass of a child's cavalry yard: friendly, tactile, a little worn. The same mat carries stitched cream roads, wooden train track and interlocking foam puzzle squares in other tile sets.

Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). All variants share one nap direction and the same green so mixed tiles never show seams.

Border material: the play-mat's hem: a 6-8 px blanket-stitched cream hem on a slightly curled felt edge that casts a thin soft shadow onto the floor beyond.

groups.title_vi: Tường - Hộp đồ chơi
groups.subject_en: Solid wall tiles for the toybox. Cap tiles are the top surface seen from above; face tiles are the short front (south-facing) vertical face that sits one row under a cap row. A north wall is one or more cap rows plus one face row; a south wall shows caps only. Wall material: the top rim of the giant toy chest wall: a dark-green painted wooden moulding with a lighter bevelled top edge, tiny brass stud heads and a worn patch of bare wood; face: vertical painted planks of the toy chest, dark green with thin darker plank seams, round brass studs in a row near the top, chipped paint at the foot.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Caps: wall_cap_a/b are the fill; edge_<side> has its outer rim on that side; corner_<dir> is an outer corner; inner_<dir> is a concave corner. Faces: a, b, c are interchangeable variants; face_end_w/e close a free end. Every wall tile is solid.

groups.title_vi: Hố / khoảng trống - Hộp đồ chơi
groups.subject_en: Gap (hole) tiles for the toybox: cells the pawn cannot walk onto but can leap over with Rule Step or bridge with the child's Chalk Path. The gap here is a gap into the dark inside of the toybox: shadowed plank walls dropping away, far below a faint glint of buried toy parts (a wheel, a tin hat) barely visible in the gloom.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Gaps never look like a floor: they are the darkest value in the district. Lips are drawn in the district's lip material. In the game camera you see the FAR (north) inner wall of a pit as a shaded vertical face about 10 px tall; the near (south) wall is hidden, so a south lip is only a thin 2-3 px highlight. End tiles (gap_end_<side>) close a trench on the named side: floor on three sides, the gap continues on the fourth. Inner-corner tiles (gap_inner_<corner>) are the concave counterpart of the outer corners: all four edge neighbours are gap and only the named diagonal neighbour is floor, so only a small notch of lip appears in that corner. Painted together with the outer corners they let any 2- or 3-cell trench and any L-, T- or plus-shaped pit be built without an open, unlit edge.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).
groups.palette_en: meadow green #5C8A3E (shade #3F6A2E), cream stitching #EFE3C2, beech wood #C89B5E, faded primary accents red #B8473D (paint only), blue #3E63A6, yellow #D8B23A; chest paint dark green #2F5B3A with brass studs #C9A24B.
groups.notes_vi: 21 ô hố: 2 ô giữa, 4 mép, 4 góc ngoài, 4 đầu mút (rãnh 3 mặt), 4 góc trong, 1 hố đơn, 2 dải. Là ô cấm đi bộ nhưng nhảy qua được. Đầu mút và góc trong cho phép ghép rãnh 2-3 ô và hố hình L/T mà không hở mép.

groups.title_vi: Vật che chắn / khối nhảy qua - Hộp đồ chơi
groups.subject_en: Low cover tiles for the toybox: solid obstacles the pawn cannot walk through but can leap over (cell kind leapable_block); they stop Rook charges and straight beams. Each reads as a district object sitting ON a floor tile.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). The tile includes its own plain floor underneath (this tile replaces the floor cell) and the object is low enough that a character behind it stays readable. A short south front face shows the object's height (about 8-10 px).
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).

groups.title_vi: Lối ra, cổng và cổng tắt - Hộp đồ chơi
groups.subject_en: Exit, gate and one-way shortcut tiles for the toybox, in open and locked states (locks are visible BEFORE they open and must read as 'blocked, and here is roughly why'). Locked and closed states are solid; open states are walkable floor.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Exit tiles sit in the room's wall ring: the wall, the opening and the floor continue seamlessly with this district's wall faces and floor tiles. An exit is named for the side of the room it leads out of. Locked tiles keep the same silhouette as the open one so the player recognises 'the same door'. groups.subject_en: Seam tiles where the toybox meets its neighbouring districts and the bedroom floor. They let rooms and the world map blend materials without hard cuts.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Seam naming: seam_to_<neighbour>_<side>: this district's floor fills the tile and the named neighbour begins along the named SCREEN side. Walkable floor.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites).

groups.title_vi: Ô sàn - Giá sách
groups.subject_en: The Bookshelf cathedral floor: big aged cream-paper pages laid flat like paving, soft off-white warming to tan at the corners, faint gutter shadow, visible paper fibres and a few creases. Printed text is only suggested as soft blurred grey bars (never legible). It reads as a hushed library at night: dry, quiet, layered.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Variants share the same paper tone and fibre pattern so a mix of them reads as one continuous page surface.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No legible titles or words on spines or pages.
groups.palette_en: paper cream #E9DDB8, aging tan #C9B27E, ink grey #55525A, shelf walnut #5A3B28, spine jewel tones oxblood #6E2B2F, navy #2D3F6B, forest #35553D, mustard #B58A2E; ribbon teal #3E7E80.

groups.subject_en: Floor edge and corner tiles for the bookshelf: they close a floor region against the out-of-board area where there is no wall (the floor's own border). Border material: the cut edge of a stack of pages: a 6-8 px band of pale layered paper edges with a yellowed tone and fine horizontal lines.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Edge naming: the suffix is the SCREEN side where the floor area ENDS (the floor continues away from that side). Corner tiles combine two sides. Inner corners are concave bends. All twelve must line up with each other and with the floor tiles on every continuing side.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No legible titles or words on spines or pages.

groups.title_vi: Tường - Giá sách
groups.subject_en: Solid wall tiles for the bookshelf. Cap tiles are the top surface seen from above; face tiles are the short front (south-facing) vertical face that sits one row under a cap row. A north wall is one or more cap rows plus one face row; a south wall shows caps only. Wall material: the top of a wall of books: the tops of upright books lined up like a battlement, cloth and leather tops with the cream page-block edge just visible between them, uneven heights; face: rows of book spines seen from the front: vertical spines in oxblood, navy, forest and mustard with plain gold bands (no titles), a thin dark shelf plank at the foot.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Caps: wall_cap_a/b are the fill; edge_<side> has its outer rim on that side; corner_<dir> is an outer corner; inner_<dir> is a concave corner. Faces: a, b, c are interchangeable variants; face_end_w/e close a free end. Every wall tile is solid.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No legible titles or words on spines or pages.
groups.palette_en: paper cream #E9DDB8, aging tan #C9B27E, ink grey #55525A, shelf walnut #5A3B28, spine jewel tones oxblood #6E2B2F, navy #2D3F6B, forest #35553D, mustard #B58A2E; ribbon teal #3E7E80.
groups.notes_vi: 19 ô tường: mũ (2 + 4 mép + 4 góc ngoài + 4 góc trong), mặt (3) và 2 đầu mặt. Tất cả là vật cản.

groups.title_vi: Hố / khoảng trống - Giá sách
groups.subject_en: Gap (hole) tiles for the bookshelf: cells the pawn cannot walk onto but can leap over with Rule Step or bridge with the child's Chalk Path. The gap here is a tear through the page: a ragged torn-paper gap whose lips are white torn fibres, dropping into shelf gloom where faint book spines can be seen very far down.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Gaps never look like a floor: they are the darkest value in the district. Lips are drawn in the district's lip material. In the game camera you see the FAR (north) inner wall of a pit as a shaded vertical face about 10 px tall; the near (south) wall is hidden, so a south lip is only a thin 2-3 px highlight. End tiles (gap_end_<side>) close a trench on the named side: floor on three sides, the gap continues on the fourth. Inner-corner tiles (gap_inner_<corner>) are the concave counterpart of the outer corners: all four edge neighbours are gap and only the named diagonal neighbour is floor, so only a small notch of lip appears in that corner. Painted together with the outer corners they let any 2- or 3-cell trench and any L-, T- or plus-shaped pit be built without an open, unlit edge.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No legible titles or words on spines or pages.
groups.palette_en: paper cream #E9DDB8, aging tan #C9B27E, ink grey #55525A, shelf walnut #5A3B28, spine jewel tones oxblood #6E2B2F, navy #2D3F6B, forest #35553D, mustard #B58A2E; ribbon teal #3E7E80.
groups.notes_vi: 21 ô hố: 2 ô giữa, 4 mép, 4 góc ngoài, 4 đầu mút (rãnh 3 mặt), 4 góc trong, 1 hố đơn, 2 dải. Là ô cấm đi bộ nhưng nhảy qua được. Đầu mút và góc trong cho phép ghép rãnh 2-3 ô và hố hình L/T mà không hở mép.

groups.title_vi: Vật che chắn / khối nhảy qua - Giá sách
groups.subject_en: Low cover tiles for the bookshelf: solid obstacles the pawn cannot walk through but can leap over (cell kind leapable_block); they stop Rook charges and straight beams. Each reads as a district object sitting ON a floor tile.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). The tile includes its own plain floor underneath (this tile replaces the floor cell) and the object is low enough that a character behind it stays readable. A short south front face shows the object's height (about 8-10 px).
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No legible titles or words on spines or pages.
groups.palette_en: paper cream #E9DDB8, aging tan #C9B27E, ink grey #55525A, shelf walnut #5A3B28, spine jewel tones oxblood #6E2B2F, navy #2D3F6B, forest #35553D, mustard #B58A2E; ribbon teal #3E7E80.
groups.notes_vi: 8 ô cover. Không che lưới: vật thấp, nhìn rõ phía sau.

groups.title_vi: Lối ra, cổng và cổng tắt - Giá sách
groups.subject_en: Exit, gate and one-way shortcut tiles for the bookshelf, in open and locked states (locks are visible BEFORE they open and must read as 'blocked, and here is roughly why'). Locked and closed states are solid; open states are walkable floor.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Exit tiles sit in the room's wall ring: the wall, the opening and the floor continue seamlessly with this district's wall faces and floor tiles. An exit is named for the side of the room it leads out of. Locked tiles keep the same silhouette as the open one so the player recognises 'the same door'. Every closed state differs clearly from its open state.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No legible titles or words on spines or pages.

groups.title_vi: Bậc thang gáy sách - Giá sách
groups.subject_en: Book-spine steps (room bs1): stacked books forming a climbing stair, each step a book lying flat with its spine facing the walker, cloth or leather binding with a gold line, the next step rising behind it.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Seen from above with a short front face: each tile shows one tread (the book's cover, 20 px deep) and one riser (the spine and page-edge, 8-10 px). The direction in the name is the way the stair RISES. The 'alt' version uses a different book colour so a flight does not repeat. Walkable floor.

Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). The ribbon is centred and exactly 10 px wide. Straight pieces join end to end. Ends are cut with a V notch. groups.title_vi: Nhà nguyện sách (bs2) - Giá sách
groups.subject_en: The Diagonal Chapel (room bs2): a cathedral of books. The floor is paper in a diagonal checker of cream and pale tan, with a red-free ribbon aisle (a deep teal carpet strip) running to an altar, and coloured light spilled by cellophane stained-glass windows.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Chapel floor tiles carry a diagonal (45 degree) lozenge pattern so the room reads as 'diagonal' without confusing the 4-way grid; the aisle is a 20 px wide teal strip with a gold border line; light patches are flat colour pools laid over the paper, drawn as the pool colour already blended into the paper pixels with a hard stepped contour (the tile stays fully opaque, no gradient). Walkable floor.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No legible titles or words on spines or pages.
groups.palette_en: paper cream #E9DDB8, tan #C9B27E, ink grey #55525A (creases and leading lines), ribbon teal #3E7E80 (the aisle), mustard gold #B58A2E (aisle border and diamond inlay). Light pools, ONE pool colour per tile: violet #7E86D8, amber #E6B85C, leaf #7BBF72, rose #D88AAE. COLOUR BUDGET: at most 10 colours per tile. Floor and aisle tiles use only the first five colours (plus at most one darker shade of cream and one of teal); a light-pool tile uses cream, tan and ink grey plus its single pool colour and that colour already blended over cream and over tan. The oxblood, navy, forest and walnut of the shelf palette are NOT used on chapel tiles.

groups.title_vi: Ô sàn - Tháp khối gỗ
groups.subject_en: The Block Tower fortress floor: the flat top faces of painted wooden toy blocks laid side by side like paving, slightly bevelled square tops with visible wood grain under worn paint and thin dark seams between blocks. It reads as solid, straight and orderly: a place that believes in rows and columns.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). One tile is one block top. Seams run along the tile border only as a thin dark inset line on two sides (north and west) so neighbouring tiles form a clean grid. Embossed marks are simple shapes only (star, arrow), never letters.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No letters or numerals on blocks or rulers; show rulers' tick marks only.

groups.title_vi: Tường - Tháp khối gỗ
groups.subject_en: Solid wall tiles for the block tower. Cap tiles are the top surface seen from above; face tiles are the short front (south-facing) vertical face that sits one row under a cap row. A north wall is one or more cap rows plus one face row; a south wall shows caps only. Wall material: the flat tops of stacked wooden blocks forming a battlement: bevelled painted tops (a mix of natural beech and faded paint) separated by thin dark seams, tiny chips; face: the front face of stacked wooden blocks, two courses high and offset like brickwork: beech and faded red, blue, yellow and green faces, chipped paint, simple embossed star and arrow marks, dark seams.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Caps: wall_cap_a/b are the fill; edge_<side> has its outer rim on that side; corner_<dir> is an outer corner; inner_<dir> is a concave corner. Faces: a, b, c are interchangeable variants; face_end_w/e close a free end. Every wall tile is solid.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No letters or numerals on blocks or rulers; show rulers' tick marks only.
groups.palette_en: natural beech #D2A669 (shade #A6783E), faded paints: red #B3473E (paint only), blue #3C5F9E, yellow #D4AF3A, green #4F8A47; dark seams #5A3E24; ruler boxwood #E4C77A with tick marks #2B2B2B.
groups.notes_vi: 19 ô tường: mũ (2 + 4 mép + 4 góc ngoài + 4 góc trong), mặt (3) và 2 đầu mặt. Tất cả là vật cản.

groups.title_vi: Hố / khoảng trống - Tháp khối gỗ
groups.subject_en: Gap (hole) tiles for the block tower: cells the pawn cannot walk onto but can leap over with Rule Step or bridge with the child's Chalk Path. The gap here is a gap between block platforms: the dark inside of the tower shaft dropping away, the sides of the blocks visible in shadow, a faint warm glimmer of floor very far below.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Gaps never look like a floor: they are the darkest value in the district. Lips are drawn in the district's lip material. In the game camera you see the FAR (north) inner wall of a pit as a shaded vertical face about 10 px tall; the near (south) wall is hidden, so a south lip is only a thin 2-3 px highlight. End tiles (gap_end_<side>) close a trench on the named side: floor on three sides, the gap continues on the fourth. Inner-corner tiles (gap_inner_<corner>) are the concave counterpart of the outer corners: all four edge neighbours are gap and only the named diagonal neighbour is floor, so only a small notch of lip appears in that corner. Painted together with the outer corners they let any 2- or 3-cell trench and any L-, T- or plus-shaped pit be built without an open, unlit edge.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No letters or numerals on blocks or rulers; show rulers' tick marks only.
groups.palette_en: natural beech #D2A669 (shade #A6783E), faded paints: red #B3473E (paint only), blue #3C5F9E, yellow #D4AF3A, green #4F8A47; dark seams #5A3E24; ruler boxwood #E4C77A with tick marks #2B2B2B.
groups.notes_vi: 21 ô hố: 2 ô giữa, 4 mép, 4 góc ngoài, 4 đầu mút (rãnh 3 mặt), 4 góc trong, 1 hố đơn, 2 dải. Là ô cấm đi bộ nhưng nhảy qua được. Đầu mút và góc trong cho phép ghép rãnh 2-3 ô và hố hình L/T mà không hở mép.

groups.subject_en: Low cover tiles for the block tower: solid obstacles the pawn cannot walk through but can leap over (cell kind leapable_block); they stop Rook charges and straight beams. Each reads as a district object sitting ON a floor tile.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). groups.title_vi: Chuyển tiếp với vùng lân cận - Tháp khối gỗ
groups.subject_en: Seam tiles where the block tower meets its neighbouring districts and the bedroom floor. They let rooms and the world map blend materials without hard cuts.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Seam naming: seam_to_<neighbour>_<side>: this district's floor fills the tile and the named neighbour begins along the named SCREEN side. Walkable floor.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No letters or numerals on blocks or rulers; show rulers' tick marks only.
groups.palette_en: natural beech #D2A669 (shade #A6783E), faded paints: red #B3473E (paint only), blue #3C5F9E, yellow #D4AF3A, green #4F8A47; dark seams #5A3E24; ruler boxwood #E4C77A with tick marks #2B2B2B.

groups.subject_en: The ruler bridge (room bt2) and its approach pieces: a giant wooden ruler laid across a gap as a bridge, boxwood yellow with black tick marks along both edges (ticks only, no numbers), a brass edge strip on one side, a hole for hanging near the end.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). The ruler is exactly 20 px wide, centred in the tile, with the void/gap visible 6 px on both long sides when used over a gap; ticks are 1 px, longer every fifth tick. groups.title_vi: Khối nứt, khối yếu và tường dễ vỡ - Tháp khối gỗ
groups.subject_en: Breakable block-tower tiles: cracked floor blocks (walkable, a warning), weak blocks (a single block the Rook can break) and breakable wall blocks, each in whole -> cracked -> rubble states. They teach 'some walls can be broken' (rooms bt3 and btb) and the Wooden Rook's collisions.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Each state must read at a glance: WHOLE = intact painted block(s); CRACKED = a bold dark zig-zag crack across the top and one chipped corner, still solid; RUBBLE = the block has broken into walkable pieces and dust on the floor tile underneath (floor, walkable). Same block colours and size across the three states of one kind.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No letters or numerals on blocks or rulers; show rulers' tick marks only.
groups.palette_en: natural beech #D2A669 (shade #A6783E), ruler boxwood #E4C77A, tick black #2B2B2B, red-paint #B3473E, blue #3C5F9E, yellow #D4AF3A, green #4F8A47, seam #5A3E24, rubble beige #B79B6E.
groups.notes_vi: Các trạng thái: nguyên - nứt - đổ nát. Khối yếu và tường dễ vỡ là vật cản cho đến khi thành đống đổ nát.

poses_en: The weak red block whole, just struck: a white flash line along the top edge and a hairline crack.
Crack opens across the face, two pieces leaning apart, dust puffs at the foot.
The block bursts into five chunks, mid-air, dust cloud thickening.
Chunks falling to the floor, dust cloud at its widest.
Rubble heap settled, a low pile of broken painted block pieces, a thin dust wisp rising.
The breakable wall block whole, struck: a white flash along the top and a hairline crack.
The block cracks through and shifts forward, dust at the sides.
The block collapses outward in several chunks, a dust cloud blooming.
Chunks tumbling to the floor, dust cloud at its widest.
Rubble heap settled across the doorway, a low pile of broken wall-block pieces.

groups.title_vi: Đỉnh tường lô cốt và bậc khối - Tháp khối gỗ
groups.subject_en: Battlement tops and block stairs of the Block Tower: crenellated tops (alternating raised merlons and low crenel gaps) built from blocks, and block stairs the pawn can climb.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Battlement tiles are seen from above with a short front face: merlon tiles are raised blocks with a 6 px front face; crenel tiles are the low gap between merlons showing only the lower course top. Stairs show one block tread and a block riser, the direction naming the way the stair RISES. All are solid (battlements) or walkable (stairs).

groups.subject_en: Floor edge and corner tiles for the dollhouse: they close a floor region against the out-of-board area where there is no wall (the floor's own border). Border material: the floor's white-painted skirting board: a 6-8 px band of white wood with gold bead trim and a thin shadow gap against the parquet.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Edge naming: the suffix is the SCREEN side where the floor area ENDS (the floor continues away from that side). Corner tiles combine two sides. Inner corners are concave bends. All twelve must line up with each other and with the floor tiles on every continuing side.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). Keep magenta flowers distinct from coral danger red.
groups.palette_en: rose pink #D58FA8 / pale pink #EBC4CF, cream #F2E6CF, plum #6B4A7C, gold trim #C9A24B, honey oak #C48B50 (shade #9C6A3A), warm lamp glow #F2C77A, lawn green #6E9B58, flower magenta #B04F86 (flowers only, never coral red).

groups.title_vi: Tường - Nhà búp bê
groups.subject_en: Solid wall tiles for the dollhouse. Cap tiles are the top surface seen from above; face tiles are the short front (south-facing) vertical face that sits one row under a cap row. A north wall is one or more cap rows plus one face row; a south wall shows caps only. Wall material: the top of a dollhouse wall: a thin lavender-painted trim cap with a gold bead line and tiny pin heads; face: rose-and-cream striped wallpaper on the upper part with tiny rosebuds, and a white-painted wainscot panel with gold beading on the lower part, resting on the skirting board.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Caps: wall_cap_a/b are the fill; edge_<side> has its outer rim on that side; corner_<dir> is an outer corner; inner_<dir> is a concave corner. Faces: a, b, c are interchangeable variants; face_end_w/e close a free end. Every wall tile is solid.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). Keep magenta flowers distinct from coral danger red.
groups.palette_en: rose pink #D58FA8 / pale pink #EBC4CF, cream #F2E6CF, plum #6B4A7C, gold trim #C9A24B, honey oak #C48B50 (shade #9C6A3A), warm lamp glow #F2C77A, lawn green #6E9B58, flower magenta #B04F86 (flowers only, never coral red).

groups.title_vi: Hố / khoảng trống - Nhà búp bê
groups.subject_en: Gap (hole) tiles for the dollhouse: cells the pawn cannot walk onto but can leap over with Rule Step or bridge with the child's Chalk Path. The gap here is a missing-floorboard gap in the dollhouse floor, revealing the dark crawlspace: painted joists in shadow and a few pale dust motes, cold and neat.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Gaps never look like a floor: they are the darkest value in the district. Lips are drawn in the district's lip material. In the game camera you see the FAR (north) inner wall of a pit as a shaded vertical face about 10 px tall; the near (south) wall is hidden, so a south lip is only a thin 2-3 px highlight. End tiles (gap_end_<side>) close a trench on the named side: floor on three sides, the gap continues on the fourth. Inner-corner tiles (gap_inner_<corner>) are the concave counterpart of the outer corners: all four edge neighbours are gap and only the named diagonal neighbour is floor, so only a small notch of lip appears in that corner. Painted together with the outer corners they let any 2- or 3-cell trench and any L-, T- or plus-shaped pit be built without an open, unlit edge.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). Keep magenta flowers distinct from coral danger red.
groups.palette_en: rose pink #D58FA8 / pale pink #EBC4CF, cream #F2E6CF, plum #6B4A7C, gold trim #C9A24B, honey oak #C48B50 (shade #9C6A3A), warm lamp glow #F2C77A, lawn green #6E9B58, flower magenta #B04F86 (flowers only, never coral red).
groups.notes_vi: 21 ô hố: 2 ô giữa, 4 mép, 4 góc ngoài, 4 đầu mút (rãnh 3 mặt), 4 góc trong, 1 hố đơn, 2 dải. Là ô cấm đi bộ nhưng nhảy qua được. Đầu mút và góc trong cho phép ghép rãnh 2-3 ô và hố hình L/T mà không hở mép.

groups.title_vi: Vật che chắn / khối nhảy qua - Nhà búp bê
groups.subject_en: Low cover tiles for the dollhouse: solid obstacles the pawn cannot walk through but can leap over (cell kind leapable_block); they stop Rook charges and straight beams. Each reads as a district object sitting ON a floor tile.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). The tile includes its own plain floor underneath (this tile replaces the floor cell) and the object is low enough that a character behind it stays readable. A short south front face shows the object's height (about 8-10 px).
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). Keep magenta flowers distinct from coral danger red.
groups.palette_en: rose pink #D58FA8 / pale pink #EBC4CF, cream #F2E6CF, plum #6B4A7C, gold trim #C9A24B, honey oak #C48B50 (shade #9C6A3A), warm lamp glow #F2C77A, lawn green #6E9B58, flower magenta #B04F86 (flowers only, never coral red).
groups.notes_vi: 8 ô cover. Không che lưới: vật thấp, nhìn rõ phía sau.

groups.subject_en: The dollhouse's little garden outside the foyer: a flocked-green lawn, flower beds of tiny paper-and-wool flowers and a pink cobble path. A toy-world garden, soft and bright.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Lawn is a flocked, slightly fuzzy short-pile green; flower beds are dark soil with pink and cream flowers; cobbles are pale pink stones with cream grout. Walkable floor. Path corner pieces (path_pink_corner_<edge><edge>) turn between the two named edges; path end pieces (path_pink_end_<side>) finish the path at the named side. PATH GEOMETRY (the same in every path file): the pink cobble path is a band exactly 16 px wide, centred on the tile (pixels 8..23 across its width); its cobbles are rounded pale pink stones about 6x6 px laid in staggered rows with 2 px cream grout lines between them, so two cobbles span the band. LAWN: flocked, slightly fuzzy short-pile green #6E9B58 with tiny paler flecks. A path piece meets a neighbouring tile with the 16 px band centred on the edge midpoint (pixels 8..23 along that edge) and lawn on both sides of it.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). Keep magenta flowers distinct from coral danger red.
groups.palette_en: rose #D58FA8, pale pink #EBC4CF, cream #F2E6CF, plum #6B4A7C, gold #C9A24B, honey oak #C48B50, stage board #A8754A, curtain plum #7A4B7E, lawn green #6E9B58, flower magenta #B04F86.
groups.notes_vi: 15 ô vườn: cỏ, hoa, lối sỏi (ngang, dọc, ngã tư, 4 góc rẽ, 4 đầu mút).

groups.title_vi: Ô sàn - Gầm giường (lâu đài đen)
groups.subject_en: The Under-Bed black castle floor: the lining of the chess box, near-black blue felt with a short matte nap, faint grey dust and a few paler fibres, occasional stitched seams. It is the darkest place in the bedroom, cool and quiet, lit only by faint warm spill from far away.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Keep value low but readable: the darkest pixel is never pure black, and there is always a tonal step between this floor and any wall or cover tile. Decorative red seams are DIM (muted wine) - bright red is reserved for the corruption hazard tiles only.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No bright red except where the description says corruption.
groups.palette_en: blue-black #14131C, charcoal #26252F (shade #1B1A26), purple blanket shadow #3A2B4F, brass #B08A3C, dim wine seam #6A2B3A (decor), dust grey #5F5C66; hazard coral #D84A3A only on corruption tiles.
groups.notes_vi: Nỉ đen lót hộp cờ: tối nhưng vẫn phải đọc được, không dùng đen tuyền.

Border material: the padded lip of the chess-box tray: a 6-8 px rolled felt lip with a line of dull brass studs and a thin dark shadow beyond.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Edge naming: the suffix is the SCREEN side where the floor area ENDS (the floor continues away from that side). Corner tiles combine two sides. Inner corners are concave bends. All twelve must line up with each other and with the floor tiles on every continuing side.

groups.title_vi: Tường - Gầm giường (lâu đài đen)
groups.subject_en: Solid wall tiles for the under-bed castle. Cap tiles are the top surface seen from above; face tiles are the short front (south-facing) vertical face that sits one row under a cap row. A north wall is one or more cap rows plus one face row; a south wall shows caps only. Wall material: the top of the chess box's wall: a polished black lacquer edge with a thin brass line, a few dust specks and cool blue reflections; face: the front face of the chess box wall: glossy black lacquer with a thin brass rule line and a dim wine seam, cool blue highlights.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Caps: wall_cap_a/b are the fill; edge_<side> has its outer rim on that side; corner_<dir> is an outer corner; inner_<dir> is a concave corner. Faces: a, b, c are interchangeable variants; face_end_w/e close a free end. Every wall tile is solid.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No bright red except where the description says corruption.
groups.palette_en: blue-black #14131C, charcoal #26252F (shade #1B1A26), purple blanket shadow #3A2B4F, brass #B08A3C, dim wine seam #6A2B3A (decor), dust grey #5F5C66; hazard coral #D84A3A only on corruption tiles.
groups.notes_vi: 19 ô tường: mũ (2 + 4 mép + 4 góc ngoài + 4 góc trong), mặt (3) và 2 đầu mặt. Tất cả là vật cản.

groups.title_vi: Hố / khoảng trống - Gầm giường (lâu đài đen)
groups.subject_en: Gap (hole) tiles for the under-bed castle: cells the pawn cannot walk onto but can leap over with Rule Step or bridge with the child's Chalk Path. The gap here is a gap into the deeper dark beneath the box: near-black void with a few drifting dust motes and one tiny dim wine glint far below.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Gaps never look like a floor: they are the darkest value in the district. Lips are drawn in the district's lip material. In the game camera you see the FAR (north) inner wall of a pit as a shaded vertical face about 10 px tall; the near (south) wall is hidden, so a south lip is only a thin 2-3 px highlight. End tiles (gap_end_<side>) close a trench on the named side: floor on three sides, the gap continues on the fourth. Inner-corner tiles (gap_inner_<corner>) are the concave counterpart of the outer corners: all four edge neighbours are gap and only the named diagonal neighbour is floor, so only a small notch of lip appears in that corner. Painted together with the outer corners they let any 2- or 3-cell trench and any L-, T- or plus-shaped pit be built without an open, unlit edge.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No bright red except where the description says corruption.
groups.palette_en: blue-black #14131C, charcoal #26252F (shade #1B1A26), purple blanket shadow #3A2B4F, brass #B08A3C, dim wine seam #6A2B3A (decor), dust grey #5F5C66; hazard coral #D84A3A only on corruption tiles.
groups.notes_vi: 21 ô hố: 2 ô giữa, 4 mép, 4 góc ngoài, 4 đầu mút (rãnh 3 mặt), 4 góc trong, 1 hố đơn, 2 dải. Là ô cấm đi bộ nhưng nhảy qua được. Đầu mút và góc trong cho phép ghép rãnh 2-3 ô và hố hình L/T mà không hở mép.

files.name: gap_inner_ne.png

In the north-east corner draw a small notch of floor about 8x8 px whose inner edge is rounded concave toward the pit, in the lip material (the rolled black felt lip with frayed fibres and a brass stud) with a 2-3 px lit rim. Directly beneath the notch the pit's far inner wall face (about 10 px tall) continues from the neighbouring east tile across the notch's 8 px width and ends in a stepped, rounded cut, so the wall face appears to wrap round the corner. Everything outside the notch is gap void with the interior and depth described in the SUBJECT. Every edge of the tile continues into gap and must match the edges of a gap centre tile.

groups.title_vi: Vật che chắn / khối nhảy qua - Gầm giường (lâu đài đen)
groups.subject_en: Low cover tiles for the under-bed castle: solid obstacles the pawn cannot walk through but can leap over (cell kind leapable_block); they stop Rook charges and straight beams. Each reads as a district object sitting ON a floor tile.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). The tile includes its own plain floor underneath (this tile replaces the floor cell) and the object is low enough that a character behind it stays readable. A short south front face shows the object's height (about 8-10 px).
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No bright red except where the description says corruption.
groups.palette_en: blue-black #14131C, charcoal #26252F (shade #1B1A26), purple blanket shadow #3A2B4F, brass #B08A3C, dim wine seam #6A2B3A (decor), dust grey #5F5C66; hazard coral #D84A3A only on corruption tiles.
groups.notes_vi: 8 ô cover. Không che lưới: vật thấp, nhìn rõ phía sau.

groups.subject_en: Exit, gate and one-way shortcut tiles for the under-bed castle, in open and locked states (locks are visible BEFORE they open and must read as 'blocked, and here is roughly why'). Locked and closed states are solid; open states are walkable floor.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Exit tiles sit in the room's wall ring: the wall, the opening and the floor continue seamlessly with this district's wall faces and floor tiles. An exit is named for the side of the room it leads out of. Locked tiles keep the same silhouette as the open one so the player recognises 'the same door'. Every closed state differs clearly from its open state.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No bright red except where the description says corruption.
groups.palette_en: blue-black #14131C, charcoal #26252F (shade #1B1A26), purple blanket shadow #3A2B4F, brass #B08A3C, dim wine seam #6A2B3A (decor), dust grey #5F5C66; hazard coral #D84A3A only on corruption tiles.

groups.subject_en: Seam tiles where the under-bed castle meets its neighbouring districts and the bedroom floor. They let rooms and the world map blend materials without hard cuts.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Seam naming: seam_to_<neighbour>_<side>: this district's floor fills the tile and the named neighbour begins along the named SCREEN side. Walkable floor.

groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). groups.title_vi: Ô bị Rule Engine ghi đè (corruption) - Gầm giường
groups.subject_en: Corruption tiles (rooms ub3 and ubb): floor cells the Rule Engine has rewritten. DORMANT tiles are felt overwritten by a grid of dim wine seams and a faint rule glyph; BURNING tiles are the damaging state, felt scored with bright coral seams and an ember glow in the cracks. Red is danger: only the burning tiles use bright coral.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Dormant: a 4x4 grid of thin dim-wine seams over the felt with one abstract glyph (a bar and a dot) in the centre, no glow. Burning: the same seams are coral and thick with orange embers in the cracks, felt charred at the edges, plus a pattern of short diagonal hatch lines so the state is not colour-only. Cell kind corruption.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No bright red except where the description says corruption.
groups.palette_en: hazard coral #D84A3A (burning only), ember orange #E58A3C, dim wine #6A2B3A, felt #1B1A26, brass #B08A3C, hot core #F4D9A0.
groups.notes_vi: Dormant là vô hại, burning là gây sát thương (có thêm gạch chéo để không chỉ dựa vào màu).

groups.title_vi: Bệ ký ức: trả lại hướng đi (ubb P3) - Gầm giường
groups.subject_en: The three memory alcove pads of the Black King's phase 3 (room ubb): a round felt pad inlaid in the floor in front of each alcove, one per direction the pawn lost (LEFT = Pebble, RIGHT = Slant, BACK = Stout). Each pad has three looks: inactive, active (the memory has returned the direction), and 'outline' (the piece was never rescued, so a blue crayon outline of it stands in).
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Each pad is a 28 px round brass-rimmed felt disc centred in the tile with a simple ivory arrow shape in the middle pointing in the direction it restores: LEFT arrow points west, RIGHT arrow east, BACK arrow south. Inactive: dim, arrow dull grey. Active: arrow warm ivory with a soft warm halo. Outline: inactive disc with a hand-drawn crayon-blue outline of the piece's silhouette (knight, bishop or rook head) next to the arrow. Walkable floor.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No bright red except where the description says corruption.

groups.title_vi: Mặt tường ký ức (ub1) - Gầm giường
groups.subject_en: The memory wall of the castle gate (room ub1): wall-face tiles of the chess box wall covered with pinned scraps of paper, tiny crayon drawings and photographs of the white pieces' good days, held by pins and bits of tape, gentle and a little sad. There are no enemies here; it is a place of remembering.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). These are wall FACE tiles (the south-facing vertical surface) that replace the plain lacquer faces; they keep the lacquer, brass rule line and foot line, and add pinned papers (cream and pale yellow) with abstract crayon marks (a sun, a house, a tiny piece silhouette), never text or readable faces. Solid.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). No bright red except where the description says corruption.
