COLOUR BUDGET: these 10 colours are the whole palette of a memory-wall tile (the separate felt, dust and card-cream tones of the old list are merged into blue-black, graphite and paper cream).

groups.subject_en: Solid wall tiles for the desk. Cap tiles are the top surface seen from above; face tiles are the short front (south-facing) vertical face that sits one row under a cap row. A north wall is one or more cap rows plus one face row; a south wall shows caps only. Wall material: the top of stacked notebooks and books: paper-edge tops (ruled-page edges), a few coloured cover tops, slightly uneven; face: the front face of stacked notebooks and hardcover books: coloured spines, ruled paper edges, spiral binding rings on the notebooks, a wooden desk shelf plank below.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Caps: wall_cap_a/b are the fill; edge_<side> has its outer rim on that side; corner_<dir> is an outer corner; inner_<dir> is a concave corner. Faces: a, b, c are interchangeable variants; face_end_w/e close a free end. Every wall tile is solid.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). Ruled-paper lines are pale blue-grey, never crayon-blue.
groups.palette_en: honey wood #B9854F (shade #9A6A3A), morning sun #F4DFA0, paper cream #EFE6CC, ruled-paper line pale blue-grey #A9BCD6 (NOT crayon blue), graphite #5D5B63, board maple #D9B77C, board walnut #6A4630.

groups.subject_en: Gap (hole) tiles for the desk: cells the pawn cannot walk onto but can leap over with Rule Step or bridge with the child's Chalk Path. The gap here is the narrow dark crack between the desk and the wall: dust, a dropped pen cap and a lost bead barely visible far down in the dark.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Gaps never look like a floor: they are the darkest value in the district. Lips are drawn in the district's lip material. In the game camera you see the FAR (north) inner wall of a pit as a shaded vertical face about 10 px tall; the near (south) wall is hidden, so a south lip is only a thin 2-3 px highlight. End tiles (gap_end_<side>) close a trench on the named side: floor on three sides, the gap continues on the fourth. Inner-corner tiles (gap_inner_<corner>) are the concave counterpart of the outer corners: all four edge neighbours are gap and only the named diagonal neighbour is floor, so only a small notch of lip appears in that corner. Painted together with the outer corners they let any 2- or 3-cell trench and any L-, T- or plus-shaped pit be built without an open, unlit edge.
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). Ruled-paper lines are pale blue-grey, never crayon-blue.
groups.palette_en: honey wood #B9854F (shade #9A6A3A), morning sun #F4DFA0, paper cream #EFE6CC, ruled-paper line pale blue-grey #A9BCD6 (NOT crayon blue), graphite #5D5B63, board maple #D9B77C, board walnut #6A4630.
groups.notes_vi: 21 ô hố: 2 ô giữa, 4 mép, 4 góc ngoài, 4 đầu mút (rãnh 3 mặt), 4 góc trong, 1 hố đơn, 2 dải. Là ô cấm đi bộ nhưng nhảy qua được. Đầu mút và góc trong cho phép ghép rãnh 2-3 ô và hố hình L/T mà không hở mép.

The east edge has no lip and no wall: it continues straight into the gap cell on the east, like the east edge of a horizontal trench strip. The interior and depth are as described in the SUBJECT: the darkest value in the district.

groups.title_vi: Vật che chắn / khối nhảy qua - Bàn học (Buổi sáng)
groups.subject_en: Low cover tiles for the desk: solid obstacles the pawn cannot walk through but can leap over (cell kind leapable_block); they stop Rook charges and straight beams. Each reads as a district object sitting ON a floor tile.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). The tile includes its own plain floor underneath (this tile replaces the floor cell) and the object is low enough that a character behind it stays readable. A short south front face shows the object's height (about 8-10 px).
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). Ruled-paper lines are pale blue-grey, never crayon-blue.
groups.palette_en: honey wood #B9854F (shade #9A6A3A), morning sun #F4DFA0, paper cream #EFE6CC, ruled-paper line pale blue-grey #A9BCD6 (NOT crayon blue), graphite #5D5B63, board maple #D9B77C, board walnut #6A4630.
groups.notes_vi: 8 ô cover. Không che lưới: vật thấp, nhìn rõ phía sau.

groups.title_vi: Bàn cờ thật và khung bàn cờ (e1) - Bàn học
groups.subject_en: The real wooden chessboard on the Desk (room e1, the playable ending): polished maple and walnut squares with a thin inlaid ivory frame line and a walnut frame around it. It is the board the whole war was about; it is calm, warm and orderly. The pawn walks to the last rank, is offered four tokens and walks off the board's edge.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels, no outline around the tile, no drop shadow outside the canvas). Floor-type tiles are mid-value, low-saturation and low-contrast so that coral-red, dark-orange, mint and crayon-blue gameplay overlays stay readable on top of them. Where a side of the tile continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side must match the district's plain floor tiles so that a grid of mixed variants shows no seams. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Board squares are 32 px, glossy wood grain (maple light, walnut dark) with a very subtle 1 px bevel on north and west. The frame tiles follow the standard edge/corner/inner convention (the suffix is the SCREEN side where the board ENDS, the frame's rim facing that side). The exit tiles show a small gap in the frame with a worn pale path where the blue crayon line leaves the board. Walkable floor (the frame rim is thin and flush).
groups.avoid_en: No characters, pieces or enemies on the tile (those are separate sprites). Ruled-paper lines are pale blue-grey, never crayon-blue.
groups.palette_en: board light maple #D9B77C (shade #B8935C), board dark walnut #6A4630 (shade #4F3322), frame walnut #4A3626, inlay ivory #E6DAC0, desk wood #B9854F, morning sun #F4DFA0.
groups.notes_vi: Bàn cờ gỗ thật: ô sáng/tối, hàng 8, khung (mép, góc ngoài, góc trong) và 4 lối thoát khỏi bàn.

groups.subject_en: Small flat floor markings that tell the player where things happen: the ring where the pawn arrives in a room, soft chevrons showing which way an exit leads, the base disc under a pickup, the yellow ring under a rescue spot and the 'reach' objective pin.
groups.details_en: Decals are transparent overlays that must work on every district's floor: pale ivory marks with a thin darker keyline so they read on both light and dark floors. Pickup glow is ivory or golden yellow, never red. Yellow = interactable. Keep marks quiet, they never compete with telegraphs.

groups.title_vi: Nét bút sáp xanh của đứa trẻ (đường chỉ dẫn)
groups.anchor: none: the decal fills its 32x32 cell (centre at (16,16)) and lies flat on the floor
groups.subject_en: The blue crayon line of the child: a hand-drawn crayon stroke that runs across tiles and across the bedroom and the board alike (the one thing that crosses both worlds). It marks a clue in room T4 (a line crossing one tile), the line the Bishop Oracle says is 'not real', and, in the ending, the path the pawn follows off the board's edge. Pieces are straight, corner, end, T and cross segments plus a dot, so a line of any shape can be built cell by cell.
groups.details_en: Each segment is the same 4 px waxy crayon stroke, centred, with the line meeting the cell edges at their midpoints so segments join seamlessly. The wax shows as slightly uneven density, tiny paper-grain gaps and a darker edge on one side. Transparent background. Only the crayon-blue colour (two tones), no outline.
groups.avoid_en: No arrowheads, no words, no extra colours, no hand, no outline, no soft glow.
groups.palette_en: crayon blue #3A6FE0 (light #8DB0F0, dark #284CA0), paper-grain gap transparent.
groups.notes_vi: 18 mảnh nét sáp xanh ghép được thành mọi đường: thẳng, lượn, góc, đầu cụt, ngã ba, chữ thập, chấm.
groups.used_in: T4, bsb P3, bs3, ending e1, hub, desk

groups.title_vi: Biểu tượng khóa: 'vì sao khóa' gắn trên cửa/cổng
groups.anchor: none: the decal fills its 32x32 cell (centre at (16,16)) and lies flat on the floor
groups.subject_en: Lock glyph plaques: a small paper tag pinned or taped beside a locked exit or gate telling, without words, what opens it. Locks are visible before they open and must explain themselves (LD.7): a toppled crown for 'beat the boss', an L-shape leap for 'needs Rule Step', a little bridge for a chalk crossing, a thick bar for 'hold the line (rub the mark)', three pawn heads for 'clear the room', a hand for 'the child lifts the latch'.
groups.details_en: Each plaque is a cream paper tag 24x28 px with a folded corner and a tiny pin or tape strip, with the drawing in thick graphite pencil only (no accent colour on any tag). The drawing must read as a simple icon at 1x. Transparent background.
groups.avoid_en: No words, no numbers, no bright red, no crayon blue (the tags are neutral world signage that stands from the first rooms, before the child is revealed).
groups.palette_en: paper cream #E9DDB8, graphite #3A3640, ivory #F1E8D2
groups.notes_vi: 7 thẻ giấy nhỏ vẽ chì: mỗi thẻ là một lý do khóa, không có chữ.
groups.used_in: hub h1 doors, every locked exit and gate

groups.title_vi: Đường Đen (Black Line) niêm phong phòng trùm
groups.anchor: none: the line fills its 32x32 cell and runs through the cell centre
groups.subject_en: The Black Line that seals a boss arena: when the pawn crosses the boundary of the 3-column antechamber, a ruler-straight black line is drawn across the floor behind it and hardens into a solid bar, so there is no retreat. After the boss falls the line fades and lifts. 'v' means the line runs north-south (it crosses an east-west path), 'h' runs east-west. Dormant = a faint dotted pencil line (the line-to-be); sealed = a solid raised black bar.
groups.details_en: Dormant: a 2 px dotted charcoal line with ruler tick marks every 8 px, flat on the floor, 50% opacity. Sealed: a 12 px thick charcoal-black bar, bevelled top edge with a cool blue-grey highlight, a short front face of 6 px on the south side, and tiny ruler tick marks along its top edge; a hairline of dim light at its base. It must read as a ruler laid down in black ink, authoritative and cold, not as fire or lava. The sealed bar is solid; the dormant line is a decoration.
groups.avoid_en: No red, no glow, no spikes, no runes, no text.
groups.palette_en: charcoal #26252F (bar), black-blue #14131C, cool highlight #6E7C95, dotted line #5A5864, floor shadow #1B1A26.
groups.notes_vi: Đường thước kẻ đen: mờ khi chưa niêm phong, thanh đen đặc khi niêm phong.
groups.used_in: b1, tbb, bsb, btb, dhb, ubb arena antechambers

groups.notes_vi: Dấu luật vẽ bằng chì: nhìn vào là biết phải tẩy đi.

groups.title_vi: Khối phấn (Chalk Block) của đứa trẻ
groups.subject_en: The child's Chalk Block: a sturdy toy block drawn in crayon-blue chalk that the huge hand sets on a free cell. It stops Rook charges, straight beams and Knight landings. It looks hand-made: rough waxy chalk strokes forming a cube with visible outline strokes, chalk dust on its top, and a few stray crayon marks. This group owns every state of the Block body: place (the hand sets it down), hold, crumble (destroyed by a charge or beam or at room end) and vanish (a new cast moves it).
groups.details_en: A cube about 24 px wide with a 12 px front face: crayon-blue chalk fill with crisscross hatch strokes, thicker outline strokes on the edges, a tiny star doodle on the front face. Cracked state: a bold dark zigzag crack and a missing chunk at one corner.

groups.anchor: centre of the floor-contact line at (16,30): the lying piece rests on the line y=30 (its lowest drawn row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it, centred on x=16
groups.subject_en: Fragments of the lost battle that dress the T1 rug around the fallen white pieces: a lone round base, a piece broken in half, a pawn's head on its own and a scatter of ivory shards. Warm ivory, rounded, repaired seams and cloth ties, tiny chips, no faces. The whole fallen pieces (pawns, knight, bishop, rook, queen) are separate files; this group only holds the fragments.
groups.details_en: Each piece lies on its side or leans, drawn from the camera angle with its round base visible; sizes follow the lying pieces (a pawn lying is 22x18 px, a knight 24x20 px). Cast shadow to the south-east. Pieces are toys: wood grain faintly visible under ivory paint. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. A piece lying on its side is its standing body box turned 90 degrees: every fragment is at most 24x20 px. Outline included, it rests on the line y=30 and is centred on x=16, so at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side and nothing touches or crosses a canvas edge; a tilted or half-fallen piece keeps its whole silhouette inside x 2..29 and y 2..29.
groups.avoid_en: No faces, no blood, no gore. No white pure fills. No black pieces here.

groups.title_vi: Bẫy giữ Pebble (Mã trắng) - hub
groups.anchor: base centre at (16,30): the same anchor as the piece sprite it covers; the trapped piece's own sprite stands in the same cell and is a separate asset
groups.subject_en: The trap holding Pebble the white Knight, a white piece in need of rescue: a big wooden toy block lying on top of the Knight's base so it cannot stand, wedged with a smaller block beside it. The block is faded yellow with chipped corners. The piece itself is drawn separately; this prop is only the trap and must leave room for the piece to be seen. Hold E for 1.5 s frees it.
groups.details_en: 32x32 canvas, exactly the cell of the piece it covers. The rescue ring on the floor is a separate decal. When the rescue completes the trap opens. LAYERING: this prop is drawn in FRONT of the piece sprite on the same 32x32 canvas with the same anchor; everything that is not part of the trap is transparent so the piece shows through, and the piece sprite never draws any part of the trap. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell): the piece under the trap is a chess piece drawn inside this cell, so the whole trap in every frame stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29 of the canvas (at least 2 px of empty canvas on every side), covers only the lower half of the piece, and never grows beyond the cell; the open and settled-aside states also stay inside the cell.

groups.details_en: 32x32 canvas, exactly the cell of the piece it covers. The rescue ring on the floor is a separate decal. When the rescue completes the trap opens. LAYERING: this prop is drawn in FRONT of the piece sprite on the same 32x32 canvas with the same anchor; everything that is not part of the trap is transparent so the piece shows through, and the piece sprite never draws any part of the trap. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell): the piece under the trap is a chess piece drawn inside this cell, so the whole trap in every frame stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29 of the canvas (at least 2 px of empty canvas on every side), covers only the lower half of the piece, and never grows beyond the cell; the open and settled-aside states also stay inside the cell.

It is the same box whose black half is the Under-Bed castle: ivory side warm and open, black side dark and shut.
groups.details_en: Open: a rectangular box 56x28 px footprint with the lid raised at the back, an ivory felt tray with eight small round slots (some empty), brass hinge and clasp, a short front face. Closed: the lid down, a brass clasp latched and a thin dark seam. Wood is dark walnut with a brass inlay line; felt is warm ivory inside.

groups.title_vi: Hộp cờ trong hub: nắp đóng lại và nắp mở ra (hoạt ảnh)
groups.subject_en: The lid of the hub's chess box in motion: a hinged dark-walnut chess box with an ivory felt tray (a rectangular box 56x28 px footprint, brass hinge and clasp, a tray of eight small round slots, a short front face), drawn here only as two short one-shot clips. LID CLOSE is the Under-Bed entry: the lid comes down and the child is cut off, the hub turns to its boxed state. LID OPEN is the end of Act 6: the box opens and the pieces become toys again. The warm light that spills out when it opens is a separate effect and the clasp hooking is a separate clip; this group is the lid itself.
groups.details_en: The same box, canvas, anchor and palette in every frame: a rectangular box 56x28 px footprint, a hinged lid, an ivory felt tray with eight small round slots, a brass hinge and clasp, a short front face. Only the lid, the clasp hook and the tray shadow change from frame to frame; the box body, the tray and every slot outline stay pixel-identical from frame to frame (wherever the lid does not cover them). The lid shadow is a flat translucent wedge in the inner shadow colour #2E2C38 at a single opacity (60 percent), never a gradient. Wood is dark walnut with a brass inlay line; felt is warm ivory.
groups.avoid_en: No light rays, no glow, no sparks, no pieces in the slots, no hand, no bright red, no text on the lid.
groups.palette_en: walnut #4A3626, brass #B08A3C, ivory felt #E6DAC0 (shade #CDBF9F), inner shadow #2E2C38.
groups.notes_vi: Hai clip cho nắp hộp cờ hub: lid_close 6 khung (S22, Gầm giường, hub thành 'boxed') và lid_open 8 khung (S24-S25, hộp mở ra).
groups.used_in: h1_chess_rug_hub (S22 the lid closes and the hub becomes boxed; S24-S25 the box opens)

poses_en: LID CLOSE 1/6: the box at rest - lid raised nearly upright at the back on its brass hinge, ivory felt tray with its eight round slots (three empty) fully visible, the brass clasp hanging open on the front face.

LID CLOSE 2/6: the lid begins to fall forward, about 70 degrees open, its ivory felt lining visible and foreshortened; a thin dark shadow wedge covers the back row of slots; the hinge barrel catches one highlight.

LID CLOSE 3/6: the lid at about 45 degrees, its felt lining a narrower band; the shadow wedge covers the back half of the tray, the slots under it keep their outlines; the front clasp starts to swing up on its hook.
LID CLOSE 4/6: the lid at about 20 degrees above the box, only a thin sliver of felt lining along its front edge; the tray is mostly in shadow; the clasp hook is raised and almost over its catch.

LID CLOSE 5/6: the lid just touching the box rim, its top face and short front face now seen; all slots hidden, only a dark crescent of shadow at the rim and a 1 px bright highlight along the lid's front edge; the lid sits 2 px lower than frame 4 for a small seating squash.
LID CLOSE 6/6: the lid shut flat and the clasp hooked over its catch, the fully closed box: a thin dark seam along the lid, no gap, no tray visible.
LID OPEN 1/8: the box fully closed - lid down, brass clasp latched, thin dark seam along the lid.
LID OPEN 2/8: the brass clasp unhooks and swings out 4 px from its catch; a 1 px dark gap opens along the front seam; nothing else has moved.
LID OPEN 3/8: the lid lifts 6 px at the front, a 2 px dark gap showing the ivory felt rim of the tray; the hinge flexes at the back.
LID OPEN 4/8: the lid at about 15 degrees open, a thin wedge of ivory felt lining and the near edge of the tray visible; a highlight runs along the hinge barrel.
LID OPEN 5/8: the lid at about 35 degrees open, more of the tray visible with the front row of slots; the back row is still hidden by the lid's felt underside.
LID OPEN 6/8: the lid at about 60 degrees open, the whole tray with all eight slots visible; the lid's felt lining foreshortened above it.
LID OPEN 7/8: the lid swings slightly past its final angle, about 100 degrees, leaning 2 px farther back than the resting pose (overshoot), a brass glint on the hinge.
LID OPEN 8/8: the lid settles back to the resting open pose - raised at the back, ivory felt tray with eight round slots (three empty) fully visible, the clasp hanging open.

groups.title_vi: Quân trắng tụ tập quanh hộp cờ (hub trạng thái 4)
groups.anchor: base centre at (16,30): the base sits on the line y=30 with 2 px of empty canvas under it
groups.subject_en: The ordinary white pawns that gather in the hub after the Queen falls: simple standing and sitting ivory pawns around the chess box, a warm small crowd of bystanders. They are decor props (not Pebble, Slant or Stout, who have their own sprites): the world has become a little safer.
groups.details_en: Pawn bodies 18x22 px at the camera angle, ivory with repaired seams; poses are 'standing facing the box', 'sitting', 'huddle' (two single-pawn files that lean toward each other when placed side by side), 'leaning' and 'waving', all in one soft idle frame. Cast shadow south-east. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. Each standing pawn body is at most 18x22 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=8 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 6 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: No faces, no weapons, no bright red.
groups.palette_en: ivory #E6DAC0, shade #CDBF9F, pale-blue seam thread #8FA6C4.
groups.notes_vi: Đám tốt trắng tụ lại quanh hộp. Cặp tốt dựa nhau được tách thành hai file một quân (A/B).

groups.title_vi: Công tắc đinh ghim (hub): Pencil đánh qua lỗ 1 ô
groups.subject_en: The hub's tack switch: a brass thumbtack standing on its head on a little round felt pad across a one-cell hole. Only a Pencil Thrust fired across the hole can push it in; that releases the latch of the nook holding the first Courage Shard (the nook is a separate prop). A quiet puzzle for the first optional verb.
groups.details_en: Up: a round brass tack head 12 px across on a 20 px felt pad with the point angled up, a bright glint. Pressed: the tack driven flat into the felt, a small ring of dust and the pad gone slightly darker with a tiny mint tick.
groups.avoid_en: Only the global avoid list applies.
groups.palette_en: brass #C9A24B (glint #F2DC9A), felt #6E8A78 pad, dust #CFC6B2, mint tick #63D68B.
groups.notes_vi: Đinh ghim đồng: bị đẩy xuống khi Pencil trúng. Hốc chứa Mảnh Dũng khí số 1 là prop riêng hub_shard_nook.

groups.title_vi: Hốc giấu Mảnh Dũng khí số 1 (hub): đóng và mở
groups.subject_en: The hub's shard nook: a small hidden cubby cut into the foot of the hub toy shelf, shut by a hinged flap of cardboard covered in rug felt, held closed by a latch that the tack switch (a separate prop) releases when a Pencil Thrust across the one-cell hole pushes the tack in. Inside is an empty felt-lined hollow where the first Courage Shard lies (the shard is its own pickup and is NOT drawn here). Closed, it reads as 'something small is kept here'; open, it is the reward the quiet puzzle promised.
groups.details_en: Closed: a 24 px wide, 20 px tall cardboard flap with a felt face, a small round brass pin-hole in its upper edge where the latch sits, a worn ribbon pull tab and a faint seam, set into a short wooden shelf foot 32 px wide and 30 px tall. Open: the flap dropped forward and flat on the floor like a little ramp (hinge at its bottom edge), the hollow behind it a felt-lined pocket in warm shadow, EMPTY, with no glow baked in (the shard pickup and its glow are separate files). The foot of the shelf is identical in both states so the two files swap cleanly.
groups.avoid_en: Only the global avoid list applies. No shard, no glow, no golden yellow (the nook is not an interactable), no text.
groups.palette_en: cardboard #C89B5E (shade #8E6D3F), rug felt #6E8A78 (shade #566E60), shelf wood #8E6D3F with grain #6E5030, brass pin #C9A24B, hollow shadow #3A3328, ribbon tab #E6DAC0.
groups.notes_vi: Hốc nhỏ dưới chân kệ đồ chơi ở hub, mở khi đinh ghim bị Pencil đẩy xuống; bên trong để trống vì Mảnh Dũng khí là pickup riêng.
groups.used_in: h1_chess_rug_hub (Courage Shard 1; opened by the hub tack switch)

groups.title_vi: Sáu cổng/lối vào các khu từ hub (khóa và mở)
groups.subject_en: The six ways out of the Chess Rug hub, each shown locked and open: Toybox, Bookshelf, Block Tower, Dollhouse, Under-Bed and the Desk. Locks are visible before they open and explain themselves through their dressing (a blocked arch, a page pile, a page tear, a velvet rope seal, a blanket drape and a ruler ramp). They sit at the hub's edges and read as parts of the bedroom: each is built from that district's own material.
groups.details_en: 64x48 canvas (2 cells wide). Each gate keeps the same silhouette in both states so the player recognises 'the same door'; the open state is clearly more open and lighter. The matching lock-glyph tag and the gap tiles are separate files.
groups.avoid_en: No text, no bright red, no characters.
groups.palette_en: each gate is built from the material colours of its own district, listed for each file.
groups.notes_vi: 6 cổng khu: mỗi cổng làm từ chất liệu của khu đó, khóa/mở cùng hình dáng.

groups.subject_en: The Toybox Gate arch (room tb1): the gateway into the Toybox kingdom, built from two sturdy wooden posts, a lintel plank and a blue banner with a horse-head emblem. A cavalry yard's entrance in toy form: proud, a little lopsided. Modular 32-wide pieces so the arch can be assembled.

A short front face on every piece. Transparent background.

Part of the toy train that is the hazard of the Toy Track Ambush (room tb3), the train crossing a row in the Knight Captain's arena (tbb) and, as a gift, the hub's state-3 train. It is a wooden-and-tin toy train: friendly, sturdy, glossy paint, brass fittings. As a hazard it must read clearly as a solid moving object with a strong silhouette; the telegraph of its lane is a separate effect.
groups.details_en: Files: the horizontal still is the part travelling EAST (left-right; mirror for west) and the vertical still is the part travelling SOUTH (top-down; mirror for north). Wheels turn through the clip frames (spoke positions alternate). Cars are exactly one cell long along their travel direction so they couple end to end with no gap.

groups.title_vi: Đèn tín hiệu đường ray, biển và thanh chắn ngang
groups.subject_en: Rail signals and level-crossing furniture of the toy track: the signal post in four states (off, warning, danger, safe), a crossing sign and the crossing arm up and down. Red here means a train is coming (danger), amber/orange means anticipation, mint means safe; these read like the telegraph language but are world props that only warn.
groups.details_en: Signal: a short beech post with a small tin lamp box on top, two lamp lenses; the lit lens glows and the other is dark. Crossing sign: a white X-shaped sign with a plain stripe pattern (no text). Crossing arm: a striped bar hinged on a post, cream and dull yellow stripes.

groups.notes_vi: Đèn tín hiệu 4 trạng thái; đỏ = tàu sắp tới.

groups.subject_en: A mirror sticker on the floor of the Bishop Oracle's arena: a shiny silver sticker laid diagonally that redirects the Oracle's beam (boss phase 2, mirrored beams that bend once). This one is the '/' orientation. Reads as 'reflective, a mirror' from the sheen alone.
groups.details_en: The sticker is a thin 4 px wide x 28 px long diagonal strip of polished silver foil with a curled corner, a bright highlight band running its length, and a faint pink-grey reflection of the page. The reflection is a pale glimmer, not a beam (beams are a separate effect). Orientation: the strip runs from the south-west corner to the north-east corner (a '/' diagonal).

groups.subject_en: Clue 3 in room bs2_diagonal_chapel: a thick adult hardcover book, far too big for the child to read, lying on a shelf with a bookmark tucked deep inside it. groups.title_vi: Khối gỗ trang trí: ký hiệu, trơn, đổ, vòm, trụ
groups.subject_en: Loose wooden toy blocks of the Block Tower as props and cover: eight symbol blocks (star, moon, heart, circle, triangle, square, diamond, arrow) and plain painted cubes, toppled blocks, an arch and a cylinder. They build the fortress and give it material identity: heavy, painted, chipped and cheerful.
groups.details_en: A block is about 24 px cube seen from above and the front: a bevelled top face, a short front face 10 px, chipped paint corners, wood grain faintly visible; symbol blocks have the shape embossed shallowly on the top face.
groups.avoid_en: No letters or numerals on blocks or rulers: use simple embossed shapes and plain tick marks.

groups.title_vi: Manh mối 4: khối có hai cái tên, một bị gạch (bt1)
groups.subject_en: Clue 4 in room bt1_block_yard: a block with two names scrawled on it in a child's pencil, one scribbled out so hard the paper-like surface is scored. It says two people were meant to be on this side and one was removed, without any words. The names are shown only as two lines of loopy pseudo-handwriting strokes (not readable text); the left line is scribbled over with a hard dark scrawl.
groups.details_en: A natural beech block 26 px wide on its side, its front face showing two horizontal lines of loopy cursive-like squiggles in graphite, the upper line crossed out by a heavy dark zig-zag scribble that tore the surface slightly. 'Inspected' state: a tiny hair of paper is lifted at the scribble and the block is turned 10 degrees.
groups.avoid_en: No readable letters.
groups.palette_en: beech #D2A669 (shade #A6783E), graphite #3A3640, scribble dark #26252F.
groups.notes_vi: Hai cái tên, một bị gạch bỏ: chỉ là nét nguệch ngoạc.

groups.title_vi: Ngai của Xe Quản ngục: nguyên, nứt, đổ nát (btb)
groups.subject_en: The Rook Warden's throne behind its lane (room btb, phase 3): a throne built of stacked blocks and rulers on a block dais, with a high straight back. In phase 3 the Rook refuses to turn and the pawn stands so that its charge smashes the throne: whole -> cracked -> rubble. The throne is made in four 32-wide parts (back, seat, left arm, right arm), each in three states.
groups.details_en: Whole: faded blocks painted red and yellow with brass-studded rulers as the back's spine, orderly and imposing; cracked: bold zig-zag cracks, a chipped corner and dust; rubble: a low heap of fragments (the back and seat gone), flat and walkable. The parts line up as: back = the tall piece in the middle row's centre; seat = in front of it; arms = left and right of the seat.

groups.title_vi: Con dấu hoàng gia (dh4, hub Dollhouse): cổng niêm phong có dấu chéo
groups.subject_en: The royal seal of the Dollhouse: a pink velvet rope between two gold posts with a large wax-and-card seal bearing the diagonal Rule Mark, sealing the way. After the Queen falls the child's hand lifts the latch and the seal opens. The pawn tries a chord (diagonal) once here and the head-shake denial plays; the seal's diagonal mark is the foreshadow of Free Step.
groups.details_en: Closed: two gold posts 40 px apart, a plump pink velvet rope in a smile curve between them, a big round plum wax seal pinned on the rope stamped with a bold diagonal line (no text); Open: the rope unhooked and lying on the floor, the seal split in two halves.

groups.subject_en: The child's drawing the Queen tears in her third phase (Tear the Drawing, which disables Believe for the phase): a crayon drawing of a little pawn pinned to the throne-room wall, whole at first and then torn in two with the pieces falling. The drawing is gentle and clumsy; the tearing is shown with paper only, no violence to anything alive.

groups.subject_en: Parts of the giant chess box that is the Under-Bed black castle: the lid's black lacquer edge, the felt inner side of the lid, hinged brass clasps (open and closed), a hinge barrel, brass corners, a blank brass label plate and a leather handle. The lid closing over the pawn is composed from the edge and inner-felt pieces and a flat shadow wedge.
groups.details_en: Lid edge: glossy black lacquer with a thin brass line and cool blue highlights; inner felt: near-black felt; clasps: dull brass hooks on a plate; hinge: a brass barrel with three screws; corners: brass L-brackets with rivets; label plate: a blank brass rectangle; handle: dark leather strap with stitching. The lid shadow piece is a flat translucent wedge: a single blue-black #14131C fill at 60% opacity (one alpha value), hard edges, tapering from its full height at the top to a point at the bottom; no gradient, no fade, no steps.
groups.avoid_en: Bright coral red is reserved for corruption hazard tiles: here use dim wine and dull brass only.
groups.palette_en: blue-black #14131C, charcoal #26252F, felt #1B1A26, plum #3A2B4F, brass #B08A3C, dim wine #6A2B3A (decor only), dust #5F5C66, card cream #D8CDB0, dim candle flame #C97B4A.

groups.subject_en: The memory wall of the castle gate: three framed memories of the rescued white pieces (Pebble the Knight, Slant the Bishop, Stout the Rook) shown as warm pinned drawings, and, for any piece the player did not rescue, a blue crayon outline of that piece drawn on the wall in place of the memory ('drawn before you'). Outline: the same frame area with only a hand-drawn crayon-blue outline of the piece's silhouette (head and body) on bare lacquer, wobbly. A 'frame empty' piece shows an empty pinned card.

groups.title_vi: Máy Rule Engine: lõi 2x2, piston, đồng hồ, cần gạt, con dấu ép
groups.subject_en: The machine of the Rule Engine in room ub3 and the Black King's arena: a big engine core made of four 32-wide quarters (a brass-and-steel drum with a dim wine window), pistons, a gauge dial with no numerals, a big lever (up and down), a fuse box and a stamp press that stamps tiles into rules. It is a rule factory: cold, tidy, patient.
groups.details_en: Core quarters nw/ne/sw/se form a 2x2 drum with a round window in the middle glowing dim wine; pistons are brass-and-steel rods on a base; gauge: a round dial with tick marks and a needle; lever: a long steel lever with a ball knob; fuse box: a grey metal box with a hinged door; stamp press: an arm with a rubber stamp face carrying an abstract rule glyph (bar and dot), up and down states.
groups.avoid_en: Bright coral red is reserved for corruption hazard tiles: here use dim wine and dull brass only.
groups.palette_en: blue-black #14131C, charcoal #26252F, felt #1B1A26, plum #3A2B4F, brass #B08A3C, dim wine #6A2B3A (decor only), dust #5F5C66, card cream #D8CDB0, dim candle flame #C97B4A.
groups.notes_vi: Cỗ máy tạo luật: lạnh và gọn gàng.

groups.subject_en: The Black King's throne in the arena (room ubb): a throne built of black lacquer and brass in five 32-wide parts (back left, back right, seat, left arm, right arm) on a dais of four edge pieces. The king is a rule system pretending to be a person: the throne is perfectly symmetrical, cold and tall.
groups.details_en: Back halves: tall symmetrical lacquer panels with a brass crown finial split between them; seat: a black felt cushion on a lacquer box; arms: lacquer scrolls; dais: layered black steps with a brass edge line (suffix is the SIDE of the dais).

groups.subject_en: Two of the objects of the six clues returned to the child's desk in room e1_morning_desk to show the shape of what the child lost without ever stating it: the big leather book with the child's bookmark now near the last page, and the block with two names where the old scribble has been overdrawn by a small crayon heart. The rest of the Desk reveal is split into single objects as separate files (the second board and its pieces, the open chess box and the pieces in its slots, the mugs, the captured-piece tray and the captured pieces). The Desk reveal references at least four earlier clues. It is quiet, domestic, a little sad and not explained.
groups.details_en: Canvas 64x64 for every file; the object sits on the base point. Big book: the leather book lying closed with the child's bookmark ribbon sticking out near the back cover; name block: the block with two names (pseudo-handwriting strokes) where the scribble has been overdrawn by a small orange crayon heart.

groups.title_vi: Quân trắng trở lại bàn cờ (kết thúc e1)
groups.anchor: base centre at (16,30): the base sits on the line y=30 with 2 px of empty canvas under it
groups.subject_en: The white pieces standing again on their squares in the ending: three ordinary white pawns and the White King upright, restored. They answer the opening (the King lying on his side) with the board put right; the rescued pieces Pebble, Slant and Stout appear through their own sprites and the rescue-flag variants. Warm ivory, the repaired seams now neat.
groups.details_en: Standing pieces seen at the camera angle: pawns 18x22 on a round base, the King 22x28 with his small cross; ivory with pale-blue stitched repair seams, tiny contact shadows; a faint warm morning light highlight on the upper-left. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell: a pawn body is at most 18x22 px and the King at most 22x28 px, centred on x=16 with the base on y=30, so at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side.
groups.avoid_en: No faces.
groups.palette_en: ivory #E6DAC0, shade #CDBF9F, seam thread #8FA6C4, morning highlight #F4DFA0.
groups.notes_vi: Quân trắng đứng lại chỗ cũ.

groups.title_vi: Node bản đồ - Act 1 (Thảm cờ vua)
groups.subject_en: World-map node images for the rooms of Act 1 (Thảm cờ vua): each one is a miniature plan view of a single room, in the room's own materials, recognisable from its landmark shapes.
groups.details_en: Flat 2D pixel art for the in-game world-map screen (a stylised plan view, not an in-room picture). Transparent background unless stated. Crisp pixels, nearest-neighbour, no anti-aliasing, 1 px darker outline in the district's darkest tone. No text, letters or numerals anywhere: names and numbers are added by the UI. Each node is a miniature plan view of one room at 56x28 px (about 3.5 px per cell of the 16x9 board; boss arenas of 18x9 cells use the same canvas): floor pattern in the room's district materials, a 2 px dark outline for the walls, key landmarks as 2-4 px shapes, the room's exits as small ivory notches in the outline on the correct sides (north = top of the image). At most 8 distinguishable shapes, readable at 1x, and every node must be recognisable by its landmark silhouette alone. Locked, boss, cleared and current states are separate overlay files, not drawn here.
groups.avoid_en: No letters or numerals, no characters or enemies (only tiny abstract shapes for landmarks), no bright red, no soft gradients.
groups.palette_en: {palette:tiles_chess_rug_floor}, plus the dark outline #2E2C38 and ivory exit notches #F1E8D2, and the child's blue crayon or chalk line #3A6FE0 only where a room description names one.
groups.notes_vi: Mỗi phòng một ảnh node 56x28; không có chữ; trạng thái khoá/hoàn thành là overlay riêng.
groups.used_in: world map screen (deferred) and tools/print_world_map.gd backdrop

Each node is a miniature plan view of one room at 56x28 px (about 3.5 px per cell of the 16x9 board; boss arenas of 18x9 cells use the same canvas): floor pattern in the room's district materials, a 2 px dark outline for the walls, key landmarks as 2-4 px shapes, the room's exits as small ivory notches in the outline on the correct sides (north = top of the image). At most 8 distinguishable shapes, readable at 1x, and every node must be recognisable by its landmark silhouette alone. Locked, boss, cleared and current states are separate overlay files, not drawn here.
groups.avoid_en: No letters or numerals, no characters or enemies (only tiny abstract shapes for landmarks), no bright red, no soft gradients.
groups.palette_en: {palette:tiles_dollhouse_floor}, plus the dark outline #2E2C38 and ivory exit notches #F1E8D2.
groups.notes_vi: Mỗi phòng một ảnh node 56x28; không có chữ; trạng thái khoá/hoàn thành là overlay riêng.

groups.title_vi: Lớp phủ trạng thái node bản đồ
groups.subject_en: State overlays for map nodes: unknown (not yet seen), seen (outline only), locked (taped shut), boss frame, optional frame, current room glow and the cleared tally tick. Combined by the UI over the room's node image.
groups.details_en: Flat 2D pixel art for the in-game world-map screen (a stylised plan view, not an in-room picture). Transparent background unless stated. Crisp pixels, nearest-neighbour, no anti-aliasing, 1 px darker outline in the district's darkest tone. No text, letters or numerals anywhere: names and numbers are added by the UI. Overlay for a map node: transparent background, drawn on top of the 56x28 node image without hiding its landmarks. Unknown: a dark paper silhouette that fully covers the node with a faint torn edge and a dotted outline (no question mark). Seen: only a thin dotted outline. Locked: two crossed strips of grey masking tape over the node. Boss frame: gold corner brackets 4 px in each corner. Optional frame: a dashed ivory border. Current: a soft ivory glow ring 2 px outside the node. Cleared: a blue crayon tally tick in the lower-right corner.
groups.avoid_en: No letters or numerals, no characters or enemies (only tiny abstract shapes for landmarks), no bright red, no soft gradients.
groups.palette_en: dark paper #26252F, outline #8C8470, masking tape grey #A8A59C, gold #C9A24B, ivory glow #FFF1B8, crayon blue #3A6FE0 (the tick).
groups.notes_vi: Các lớp phủ: chưa biết, đã thấy, khóa, trùm, tùy chọn, hiện tại, đã dọn.

groups.details_en: Flat 2D pixel art for the in-game world-map screen (a stylised plan view, not an in-room picture). Transparent background unless stated. Crisp pixels, nearest-neighbour, no anti-aliasing, 1 px darker outline in the district's darkest tone. No text, letters or numerals anywhere: names and numbers are added by the UI. The frame is a homemade cardboard frame of a child's map: brown cardboard with a crayon-scribble border, strips of masking tape at the corners and a few drawing-pin heads. Repeating 32x16 strips that tile seamlessly left-right.
groups.avoid_en: No letters or numerals, no characters or enemies (only tiny abstract shapes for landmarks), no bright red, no soft gradients.
groups.palette_en: cardboard #B8935C, crayon accents.
groups.notes_vi: Cạnh ngang lặp được.

groups.title_vi: Ô thảm cờ khuyết (màn hình chính sau khi hoàn thành)
groups.subject_en: The one-square-missing tile of the title board after the game is completed (the title shows the Rug board with one square empty): a clean square hole in the rug showing the dusk wooden floor beneath, with the cut rug edge frayed by a thin line of wool fibres on all four sides. Quiet and a little sad, never damage.
groups.details_en: Exactly 32x32 px, fully opaque, the art fills the whole canvas edge to edge (no transparent pixels except where this description says a hole shows the floor below, no outline around the tile). Seen from directly above. Edge and corner names use compass directions of the SCREEN (north = top of the tile). Where a side continues into neighbouring floor, the pixels on that side match the district's plain floor tiles so mixed variants show no seams. Walkable floor. The hole is fully opaque: the floor below is painted into the tile (no transparency).
groups.avoid_en: a piece standing in the hole, a crayon mark, red, a hard black void
groups.palette_en: dusk floorboards #4A3828 / #6B4A32, cut rug edge ivory #E6DAC0 / charcoal #3F3D4A, fibres #CDBF9F
groups.notes_vi: Một ô khuyết trên thảm, nhìn thấy sàn gỗ bên dưới.
